data.objective: Reduce normal-path latency from committed workflow lifecycle event to foreground notification-bell update to P95 at or below 2 seconds for approximately 200 concurrent foreground users.

requirements.statement: A committed workflow lifecycle event must be dispatched immediately by eventId and reflected by a one-second foreground unread-count poll so normal-path end-to-end notification latency is P95 <= 2 seconds.
acceptance: At least 20 real event runs measure P95 <= 2 seconds from event transaction commit to browser bell-count update
The immediate path does not wait for the five-second scheduled scan
The foreground unread-count polling base interval is one second
requirements.source: User confirmed the two-second P95 target and selected immediate after-commit dispatch plus frontend polling on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: Lifecycle notifications remain dependent on the five-second scheduler
The foreground notification center continues polling every fifteen seconds

requirements.statement: Immediate dispatch must occur only after a successful transaction commit and its failure must never roll back or change the committed workflow action.
acceptance: A rolled-back event transaction produces no notification dispatch
A failing notification consumer leaves the workflow approval result successful and durable
The failed delivery remains available for scheduled compensation
requirements.source: User-confirmed reliability design on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: Notification failure causes approval rollback
An event from a rolled-back transaction is delivered

requirements.statement: Immediate and scheduled delivery paths must atomically claim each delivery row before invoking a consumer, preserving one consumer call during normal races and idempotent effects during crash recovery.
acceptance: Concurrent immediate and scheduled attempts on one delivery result in exactly one successful claim and one consumer call
A process crash after consumer success but before status persistence may retry, but existing consumer idempotency produces one business effect and one notification
requirements.source: User-confirmed architecture and reliability design on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: Both paths select PENDING and invoke the consumer before either updates status
Crash recovery creates duplicate user notifications

requirements.statement: Immediate failures and stale claimed deliveries must automatically return to the durable scheduled path while retaining the existing five-attempt and DEAD semantics.
acceptance: An immediate failure returns the delivery to schedulable PENDING and a later scheduled pass can deliver it
A DISPATCHING row older than the recovery threshold is reclaimed without manual database editing
Repeated scheduled failure reaches DEAD on the fifth attempt and manual retry remains compatible
requirements.source: User-confirmed failure and recovery design on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: A delivery remains permanently DISPATCHING after interruption
Immediate dispatch failure discards the durable event

requirements.statement: Unread polling must run only while the document is visible, refresh immediately on visibility restoration, focus, and drawer open, and prevent overlapping count requests.
acceptance: Hidden documents issue no periodic unread-count requests
Visibility restoration, focus, and drawer open cause an immediate refresh
A slow unread-count request never overlaps another count request
A changed count refreshes list and module summaries only when the drawer is open
requirements.source: User-confirmed frontend polling design on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: Background tabs continue polling once per second
Slow responses accumulate concurrent polling requests
The full notification list reloads every second while the drawer is closed

requirements.statement: Consecutive silent unread-count failures must back off to 2, 5, and 15 seconds without repeated user-facing errors, and reset to one second after success or foreground restoration.
acceptance: Observed retry intervals follow 2s, 5s, and 15s on consecutive failures
Background failures do not repeatedly display error messages
A successful refresh, focus, or visibility restoration resets the base interval to one second
requirements.source: User-confirmed degradation design on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: A failed endpoint is retried every second indefinitely
Every silent polling failure displays a toast

requirements.statement: The existing authenticated unread-count endpoint must sustain approximately 200 requests per second from 200 foreground users.
acceptance: Two hundred concurrent clients poll for 60 seconds with zero request errors
Unread-count API response-time P95 is <= 200ms under that load
Database connection-pool exhaustion and application error logs are absent during the run
requirements.source: User confirmed approximately 200 foreground users and the performance acceptance on 2026-08-18.
counterexample: The implementation meets latency only by exceeding database or connection-pool capacity
The load run contains request errors or API P95 above 200ms

invariants: Workflow lifecycle events and delivery rows remain durable in the same business transaction
Rolled-back business transactions do not emit notifications
Notification failure never changes a committed workflow result

Tenant and user scoping continue to come from the authenticated server principal

interfaces.contract: Dispatch only delivery rows belonging to eventId; each row must be atomically claimed before consumer invocation; exceptions are contained from the business result.

interfaces.contract: Claim due PENDING/RETRY rows and stale DISPATCHING rows using the same state machine as the immediate path.

interfaces.name: GET /api/notifications/unread-count

error_handling.recovery: The business caller handles the original transaction failure; there is no notification delivery to recover.

error_handling.recovery: The existing five-second scheduler retries through the durable delivery record.

error_handling.behavior: The row remains DISPATCHING until its updated_at exceeds the configured threshold.
error_handling.recovery: Scheduled recovery returns it to retryable processing; consumer idempotency suppresses duplicate effects.

error_handling.behavior: The last successful badge remains and silent polling backs off to 2, 5 and 15 seconds without repeated toasts.
error_handling.recovery: Success, focus or visibility restoration resets polling to one second.

assumptions.text: Approximately 200 users means 200 simultaneously visible foreground pages and therefore approximately 200 unread-count requests per second.
assumptions.basis: User supplied the concurrency scale and selected one-second polling.
assumptions.falsifier: Measured foreground concurrency materially exceeds 200 users.

assumptions.text: Lifecycle consumers are local, short-running and idempotent.
assumptions.basis: Current consumers run in-process; notification publication has an event idempotency key and release lifecycle consumption tracks receipts.
assumptions.falsifier: A consumer performs long external I/O or cannot tolerate replay after a crash.

assumptions.text: A default 60-second stale-claim threshold is safely above normal lifecycle-consumer duration.
assumptions.basis: Current consumers perform local database work expected to complete well below one minute.
assumptions.falsifier: Focused timing tests show legitimate consumer execution approaching or exceeding 60 seconds.

decisions.decision: Use normal-path P95 <= 2 seconds as the user-visible latency objective.
decisions.reason: It is measurable and allows exceptional failure/recovery paths to remain durable rather than falsely promising a hard deadline.

decisions.decision: Trigger specific lifecycle deliveries immediately after commit and retain the scheduler as compensation.
decisions.reason: This removes the known five-second wait without weakening transaction durability or recovery.
decisions.source: User selected option 1 and confirmed the architecture on 2026-08-18.

decisions.decision: Poll the existing unread-count endpoint every second only while foreground-visible.
decisions.reason: At the confirmed 200-user scale it meets the latency target with less infrastructure than push connections.
decisions.source: User selected option 1 and confirmed approximately 200 users on 2026-08-18.

decisions.decision: Use atomic delivery-row claiming and updated_at-based stale recovery without a schema migration.
decisions.reason: The current VARCHAR status and timestamp fields already support the required state machine and recovery signal.
decisions.source: User confirmed the reliability design on 2026-08-18.

decisions.decision: Back off silent frontend failures to 2, 5 and 15 seconds and reset on success or foreground restoration.
decisions.reason: This protects the server during faults while preserving immediate recovery for active users.
decisions.source: User confirmed the frontend degradation design on 2026-08-18.

risks.risk: Actual foreground concurrency or polling fan-out exceeds the confirmed 200-user baseline.
risks.impact: Unread-count database and connection-pool load may exceed the measured capacity.
risks.mitigation: Run the required load test, observe pool and query latency, and separately review caching or push only if measured demand exceeds the baseline.

risks.risk: The stale-claim threshold is shorter than a legitimate consumer execution.
risks.impact: A second worker may replay a still-running consumer.
risks.mitigation: Default to 60 seconds, make the threshold configurable, measure consumer duration and retain consumer idempotency.

risks.risk: Synchronous after-commit dispatch extends request-thread occupancy.
risks.impact: Business API latency or throughput may degrade even though the transaction is already committed.
risks.mitigation: Dispatch only the specific event through local consumers, measure business response latency, and introduce a bounded existing-stack executor only if measurements require it.

risks.risk: Parallel dirty-worktree changes overlap the same dispatcher or notification-center files.
risks.impact: A broad edit could overwrite unrelated work or create hard-to-review conflicts.
risks.mitigation: Re-read current files before implementation, apply minimal patches and never reset or clean the worktree.

tasks.goal: Provide after-commit event-specific dispatch with atomic claim, compensation and stale recovery.
input_facts: WorkflowLifecycleEventService writes event and delivery rows in caller transactions.
WorkflowLifecycleDispatcher currently selects PENDING/RETRY every five seconds and consumes before a claim.
The existing delivery table can represent DISPATCHING and stale recovery without a migration.
invariants: Event and delivery rows commit before dispatch.
Notification failure never changes a committed workflow result.
The scheduler, five attempts, DEAD and manual retry remain compatible.
Unrelated dirty-worktree changes remain untouched.
interface_contracts: dispatchEvent(String eventId) handles only matching due deliveries.
Only a successful PENDING/RETRY to DISPATCHING conditional update authorizes consumption.
Successful consumption changes DISPATCHING to DELIVERED; immediate failure returns to schedulable PENDING.
Stale DISPATCHING is recovered by updated_at and remains replay-idempotent.
non_goals: No schema, API, queue, cache or lifecycle-consumer contract change.
action_bounds: Modify only the two lifecycle services and their direct tests.
Keep the default scheduler delay at five seconds and stale threshold at sixty seconds.
Do not alter business workflow state transitions or notification payloads.
acceptance: Commit dispatches immediately and rollback does not dispatch.
Immediate/scheduled normal race invokes one consumer.
Immediate failure does not escape and remains schedulable.
Stale claim recovers and fifth scheduled failure reaches DEAD.
Workflow Maven tests pass.
evidence_required: Focused and module Maven commands with exit codes
tasks.rollback: Revert only T1 service and test changes; the existing scheduler remains.
stop_conditions: A consumer is not replay-idempotent
A schema change is required
Immediate dispatch can observe incomplete business state
escalation_conditions: A queue, public event-contract change or retry-semantic change becomes necessary

tasks.goal: Provide visibility-aware one-second unread polling with request de-duplication and failure backoff.
input_facts: UiNotificationCenter uses a 15000ms setInterval and focus refresh.
The existing unread-count endpoint and list/module request version guards are reusable.
The frontend has no unit-test framework and must retain its current public template contract.
invariants: Notification API, DTO, display, filter, read and navigation semantics remain unchanged.
Hidden pages issue no periodic count requests.
Only one unread-count request may be in flight.
Unrelated component edits remain untouched.
interface_contracts: Visible successful polling waits one second after request completion.
Focus, visibility restoration and drawer open trigger or reuse an immediate count request.
Failures back off at two, five and fifteen seconds without repeated toast.
List and module summaries refresh only when the drawer is open and the count changed.
non_goals: No API, store, global poller, dependency, push transport or UI redesign.
action_bounds: Modify only the script section lifecycle needed for polling.
Preserve existing request-version guards and visible error behavior.
Use browser-native visibility/focus events and setTimeout.
acceptance: Frontend production build passes.
Code no longer contains the 15000ms fixed interval.
Visible, hidden, focus, drawer, in-flight and backoff paths match R5-R6.
Existing notification drawer behavior remains usable.

stop_conditions: API or DTO changes become necessary

feedback.expected: 200 clients for 60 rounds with zero errors and unread-count API P95 <= 200ms without pool exhaustion or application errors.
feedback.observed: 12000/12000 requests succeeded with no pool or application errors, but API P95 was 221.407ms.
feedback.evidence: Load test p50=109.63ms, p95=221.407ms, p99=343.717ms, max=420.491ms; MySQL Max_used_connections=21 and Threads_running=2.
feedback.sensor_limit: Single local-machine end-to-end sample includes authentication identity hydration and avatar URL presigning.
feedback.causal_hypothesis: Hypothesis: repeated AuthService.me() identity hydration and MinIO avatar URL presigning in JwtAuthenticationFilter contributes enough fixed request cost to exceed 200ms P95.
feedback.correction_check: Rerun the same 200-client, 60-round authenticated load test after an authorized bounded security-path optimization; require zero errors and P95 <= 200ms.
feedback.decision_reason: R7 is measurably above 200ms P95. The smallest plausible correction touches server/src/platform/security/**, explicitly read-only under REQ-20260818-035, so separate authorization or a scope revision is required.
